question: List the names of all stations in Lyon, in alphabetical order.
gold_sql: SELECT name FROM station WHERE city = 'Lyon' ORDER BY name

question: How many bikes have the status 'maintenance'?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bike WHERE status = 'maintenance'

question: How many members joined in 2025?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM member WHERE joined_on >= '2025-01-01' AND joined_on <= '2025-12-31'

question: What is the average trip distance in km, rounded to 2 decimal places?
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(distance_km), 2) FROM trip

question: How many maintenance records have not been resolved yet?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM maintenance WHERE resolved_on IS NULL

question: List the 3 cheapest plans by monthly fee, giving the plan name and the fee.
gold_sql: SELECT name, monthly_fee FROM plan ORDER BY monthly_fee ASC LIMIT 3

question: What is the total amount paid with the method 'card'?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payment WHERE method = 'card'

question: How many trips did not end at any station?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trip WHERE end_station_id IS NULL

question: Give the trip_id and distance of the 5 longest trips by distance, longest first.
gold_sql: SELECT trip_id, distance_km FROM trip ORDER BY distance_km DESC, trip_id ASC LIMIT 5

question: What is the largest battery capacity in Wh among electric models?
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(battery_wh) FROM model WHERE is_electric = 1

question: For each station, give the station name and the number of bikes currently assigned to it. Include stations that have no bikes, with a count of 0.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, COUNT(b.bike_id) FROM station s LEFT JOIN bike b ON b.station_id = s.station_id GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name

question: For each plan, give the plan name and the total amount paid by members on that plan. Include every plan, even those whose members have made no payments; use 0 for those.
gold_sql: SELECT p.name, COALESCE(SUM(pay.amount), 0) FROM plan p LEFT JOIN member m ON m.plan_id = p.plan_id LEFT JOIN payment pay ON pay.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY p.plan_id, p.name

question: Which manufacturer has the most bikes in the fleet? Give the manufacturer name only.
gold_sql: SELECT mo.manufacturer FROM bike b JOIN model mo ON mo.model_id = b.model_id GROUP BY mo.manufacturer ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

question: For each station that at least one trip started from, give the station name and the average distance of those trips, rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, ROUND(AVG(t.distance_km), 2) FROM trip t JOIN station s ON s.station_id = t.start_station_id GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name

question: How many trips ended at a station different from the one they started at? Trips that did not end at any station do not count.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trip WHERE end_station_id IS NOT NULL AND end_station_id <> start_station_id

question: For each model, give the model name and the number of maintenance records for bikes of that model. Include models with no maintenance records, with a count of 0.
gold_sql: SELECT mo.name, COUNT(ma.maint_id) FROM model mo LEFT JOIN bike b ON b.model_id = mo.model_id LEFT JOIN maintenance ma ON ma.bike_id = b.bike_id GROUP BY mo.model_id, mo.name

question: Which cities have more than 2 stations? Give the city and the station count.
gold_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM station GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) > 2

question: For each station that has at least one bike with a maintenance record, give the station name and the total resolved maintenance cost of bikes assigned to it. Ignore unresolved records, which have no cost.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, SUM(ma.cost) FROM maintenance ma JOIN bike b ON b.bike_id = ma.bike_id JOIN station s ON s.station_id = b.station_id WHERE ma.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name

question: How many members who joined in 2025 have made at least one payment?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) FROM member m JOIN payment p ON p.member_id = m.member_id WHERE m.joined_on >= '2025-01-01' AND m.joined_on <= '2025-12-31'

question: For each payment method, give the method, the number of payments and the total amount.
gold_sql: SELECT method, COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY method

question: Give the model name and the total distance ridden for the 3 models with the highest total distance, highest first.
gold_sql: SELECT mo.name, SUM(t.distance_km) FROM trip t JOIN bike b ON b.bike_id = t.bike_id JOIN model mo ON mo.model_id = b.model_id GROUP BY mo.model_id, mo.name ORDER BY SUM(t.distance_km) DESC LIMIT 3

question: Give the member_id and total amount paid for every member whose total payments exceed 300.
gold_sql: SELECT member_id, SUM(amount) FROM payment GROUP BY member_id HAVING SUM(amount) > 300

question: How many trips started in each month of 2025? Give the month as YYYY-MM and the number of trips.
gold_sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', started_at) AS m, COUNT(*) FROM trip WHERE started_at >= '2025-01-01' AND started_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY m

question: What is the average monthly fee of the plans held by members living in Lille, rounded to 2 decimal places?
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.monthly_fee), 2) FROM member m JOIN plan p ON p.plan_id = m.plan_id WHERE m.city = 'Lille'

question: For each station, give the station name and the number of bikes assigned to it whose status is 'retired'. Include stations with none, with a count of 0.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, COUNT(b.bike_id) FROM station s LEFT JOIN bike b ON b.station_id = s.station_id AND b.status = 'retired' GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name

question: Give the member_id and full name of every member who has referred at least 3 other members, together with the number of people they referred.
gold_sql: SELECT m.member_id, m.full_name, COUNT(r.member_id) FROM member m JOIN member r ON r.referred_by = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.full_name HAVING COUNT(r.member_id) >= 3

question: For each station, give the station name, the number of trips that started there and the number of trips that ended there. Include every station.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trip t WHERE t.start_station_id = s.station_id), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trip t WHERE t.end_station_id = s.station_id) FROM station s

question: Give the member_id of every member whose average trip distance is greater than the average trip distance across all trips.
gold_sql: SELECT member_id FROM trip GROUP BY member_id HAVING AVG(distance_km) > (SELECT AVG(distance_km) FROM trip)

question: Which model has the highest total resolved maintenance cost per bike owned? Give the model name and that ratio rounded to 2 decimal places. Consider only models that have at least one maintenance record.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT b.model_id, SUM(ma.cost) AS total FROM maintenance ma JOIN bike b ON b.bike_id = ma.bike_id WHERE ma.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.model_id), n AS (SELECT model_id, COUNT(*) AS fleet FROM bike GROUP BY model_id) SELECT mo.name, ROUND(c.total / n.fleet, 2) FROM c JOIN n ON n.model_id = c.model_id JOIN model mo ON mo.model_id = c.model_id ORDER BY c.total / n.fleet DESC LIMIT 1

question: For each plan, give the plan name and the percentage of its members who have taken at least one trip, rounded to 1 decimal place. Include every plan.
gold_sql: SELECT p.name, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT t.member_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id), 1) FROM plan p JOIN member m ON m.plan_id = p.plan_id LEFT JOIN trip t ON t.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY p.plan_id, p.name

question: Give the member_id of every member who has made at least one payment but has never taken a trip.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM payment WHERE member_id NOT IN (SELECT member_id FROM trip)

question: For each station that has at least one resolved maintenance record on an assigned bike, give the station name and the longest number of days between a maintenance report and its resolution.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, MAX(julianday(ma.resolved_on) - julianday(ma.reported_on)) FROM maintenance ma JOIN bike b ON b.bike_id = ma.bike_id JOIN station s ON s.station_id = b.station_id WHERE ma.resolved_on IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name

question: Give the member_id and full name of every member who joined in 2024 and whose first trip happened more than 120 days after they joined.
gold_sql: SELECT m.member_id, m.full_name FROM member m JOIN trip t ON t.member_id = m.member_id WHERE m.joined_on >= '2024-01-01' AND m.joined_on <= '2024-12-31' GROUP BY m.member_id, m.full_name HAVING julianday(MIN(t.started_at)) - julianday(m.joined_on) > 120

question: Give the member_id of every member who took trips in at least 4 different calendar months of 2025.
gold_sql: SELECT member_id FROM trip WHERE started_at >= '2025-01-01' AND started_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY member_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', started_at)) >= 4

question: Give the member_id of every member who has started trips from stations in all 5 cities.
gold_sql: SELECT t.member_id FROM trip t JOIN station s ON s.station_id = t.start_station_id GROUP BY t.member_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.city) = 5

question: For each model, give the model name and the percentage of its bikes that have at least one maintenance record, rounded to 1 decimal place. Include every model.
gold_sql: SELECT mo.name, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.bike_id IN (SELECT bike_id FROM maintenance) THEN b.bike_id END) / COUNT(DISTINCT b.bike_id), 1) FROM model mo JOIN bike b ON b.model_id = mo.model_id GROUP BY mo.model_id, mo.name

question: Give the bike_id of every bike whose most recent maintenance record is unresolved.
gold_sql: SELECT bike_id FROM maintenance ma WHERE reported_on = (SELECT MAX(reported_on) FROM maintenance x WHERE x.bike_id = ma.bike_id) AND resolved_on IS NULL

question: Give the member_id of every member who has taken 2 or more trips on the same calendar day.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT member_id FROM (SELECT member_id, date(started_at) AS d FROM trip GROUP BY member_id, date(started_at) HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2)

question: Give the member_id of the referred member and the member_id of their referrer, for every pair where both live in the same city.
gold_sql: SELECT b.member_id, a.member_id FROM member a JOIN member b ON b.referred_by = a.member_id WHERE a.city = b.city

question: For each city, give the city and the member_id of the member who has started the most trips from stations in that city, with their trip count. Break ties by the lower member_id. Order by city name.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT s.city AS city, t.member_id AS mid, COUNT(*) AS n FROM trip t JOIN station s ON s.station_id = t.start_station_id GROUP BY s.city, t.member_id), r AS (SELECT city, mid, n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY n DESC, mid ASC) AS rk FROM c) SELECT city, mid, n FROM r WHERE rk = 1 ORDER BY city

question: For each month of 2025, give the month as YYYY-MM, the number of trips, and the change in trip count compared with the previous month. The first month has no previous month, so its change is NULL. Order by month.
gold_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', started_at) AS mo, COUNT(*) AS n FROM trip WHERE started_at >= '2025-01-01' AND started_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY mo) SELECT mo, n, n - LAG(n) OVER (ORDER BY mo) FROM m ORDER BY mo

question: Give the trip_id of every trip whose distance is more than twice the average distance of all trips starting from the same station.
gold_sql: SELECT t.trip_id FROM trip t WHERE t.distance_km > 2 * (SELECT AVG(x.distance_km) FROM trip x WHERE x.start_station_id = t.start_station_id)

question: Give the station name and the share of trips starting there that ended at a different station, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place. Trips that did not end at any station count in the denominator but not the numerator.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.end_station_id IS NOT NULL AND t.end_station_id <> t.start_station_id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM trip t JOIN station s ON s.station_id = t.start_station_id GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name

question: Give the 2 models with the most trips within each manufacturer: the manufacturer, the model name and the trip count. Break ties by model name ascending. Order by manufacturer then trip count descending.
gold_sql: WITH c AS (SELECT mo.manufacturer AS man, mo.name AS nm, COUNT(*) AS n FROM trip t JOIN bike b ON b.bike_id = t.bike_id JOIN model mo ON mo.model_id = b.model_id GROUP BY mo.model_id, mo.manufacturer, mo.name), r AS (SELECT man, nm, n, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY man ORDER BY n DESC, nm ASC) AS rk FROM c) SELECT man, nm, n FROM r WHERE rk <= 2 ORDER BY man, n DESC

question: Give the member_id and the number of days between their first and last trip, for members where that gap is more than 500 days.
gold_sql: SELECT member_id, julianday(MAX(started_at)) - julianday(MIN(started_at)) FROM trip GROUP BY member_id HAVING julianday(MAX(started_at)) - julianday(MIN(started_at)) > 500

question: Give the bike_id of every bike that has never been ridden by a member on the Premium plan.
gold_sql: SELECT bike_id FROM bike WHERE bike_id NOT IN (SELECT t.bike_id FROM trip t JOIN member m ON m.member_id = t.member_id JOIN plan p ON p.plan_id = m.plan_id WHERE p.name = 'Premium')

question: Which maintenance issue has the highest average resolution time in days? Give the issue and that average rounded to 2 decimal places, considering only resolved records.
gold_sql: SELECT issue, ROUND(AVG(julianday(resolved_on) - julianday(reported_on)), 2) AS a FROM maintenance WHERE resolved_on IS NOT NULL GROUP BY issue ORDER BY a DESC LIMIT 1

question: Give the 5 busiest calendar days of 2025 by number of trips started: the date as YYYY-MM-DD and the trip count, busiest first. Break ties by date ascending.
gold_sql: SELECT date(started_at) AS d, COUNT(*) AS n FROM trip WHERE started_at >= '2025-01-01' AND started_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY d ORDER BY n DESC, d ASC LIMIT 5

question: For each city, give the city and the total resolved maintenance cost of bikes assigned to stations in that city. Include every city that has at least one station, using 0 where there is no cost.
gold_sql: SELECT s.city, COALESCE(SUM(ma.cost), 0) FROM station s LEFT JOIN bike b ON b.station_id = s.station_id LEFT JOIN maintenance ma ON ma.bike_id = b.bike_id AND ma.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.city

question: Give the station name of every station whose number of assigned bikes is more than half its capacity.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name FROM station s JOIN bike b ON b.station_id = s.station_id GROUP BY s.station_id, s.name, s.capacity HAVING COUNT(b.bike_id) > s.capacity / 2.0
